The Variable Rule Decides Which Fractional Variable to Split
Strong Branching Buys a Smaller Tree With Extra LPs

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-memory: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-memory: Depth-first never had more than 14 nodes waiting. Each step down the tree leaves one sibling waiting, so the list holds at most about one node per level of the current path, and a 0-1 tree on 40 variables has at most 40 levels. Memory stays small no matter how big the tree grows.
recorded.prompt:q-most-fractional: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-most-fractional: **Most fractional** takes the variable whose value is closest to 0.5: `min(v, 1 - v)` is its distance to the nearer of 0 and 1, and the rule takes the largest.
recorded.prompt:q-strong: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-strong: It takes the candidate with the largest product of its two drops. ... The product prefers x_b. (Here 30 x 0.5 = 15 for x_a and 6 x 5 = 30 for x_b.)

recorded.prompt:q-memory:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-memory:b: Breadth-first solves every node of one depth before any node of the next. It took 10,425 nodes and held 3,366 waiting. ... Breadth-first is the rule to avoid.
recorded.prompt:q-memory:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-memory:c: Memory follows the node rule, not the variable rule. Whatever the variable rule, depth-first kept at most 15 nodes waiting, best-first between 72 and 504, and breadth-first between 1,259 and 3,366. (breadth/most: 2,839 most waiting)
recorded.prompt:q-memory:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-memory:d: Memory follows the node rule, not the variable rule. ... A better variable rule shrinks best-first's list, but it stays far above depth-first's. (Table: best/first 504 most waiting, the largest of the best-first runs, so switching to first fractional does not shrink it.)

recorded.outcome:q-strong:d: Every choice is correct, since every split keeps all plans (lesson 3.2.1); the choice changes how fast the bounds fall. Strong branching scores the candidates and picks one.
